core_design_principle.rule: NPS returns are market-linked, not fixed. No official fixed 'NPS rate' exists; a simulator must derive returns from actual historical NAV series per scheme/PFM.

citation.quote: NPS does not offer any fixed returns. The returns under NPS are market-linked.

asset_classes.name: Alternative Investment Funds (REITs, InvITs, CMBS, MBS, AIFs etc.), capped at 5% of a subscriber's allocation

list: ICICI Prudential Pension Fund Mgmt Co. Ltd. (PFM007)
Aditya Birla Sun Life Pension Management Ltd. (PFM010)
DSP Pension Fund Managers Pvt. Ltd. (PFM014)
pension_fund_managers_current.note: Max Life Pension Fund Management Ltd. (PFM012) schemes were discontinued w.e.f. 18-04-2025 per regulatory direction; excluded from current NAV feeds (confirmed absent from live nav-report-excel dump taken 2026-09-27).

government_sector: Corporate CG (legacy, closed to new corporate subscribers)
NPS Lite / Swavalamban (informal sector, largely superseded by APY)
UPS CG / UPS Pool CG (Unified Pension Scheme, from 1 April 2025)
all_citizen_and_corporate: E/C/G Tier II (Active Choice, plus Tier II Tax Saver Scheme 'TTS' for Central Govt employees only)
Auto Choice / Lifecycle common schemes: Life Cycle 25-Low, Life Cycle 50-Moderate, Life Cycle 75-High, Life Cycle-Aggressive (renamed from LC25/LC50/LC75/BLC, see lifecycle_funds below)
NPS Sanchay (composite, govt-sector-like allocation, for informal-sector/other subscribers)

Multiple Scheme Framework (MSF) schemes - ~20 PFM-branded schemes approved from Sept 2025 (e.g. SBI NPS Jeevan Swarna Retirement Yojana, SBI NPS Akshay Dhara, HDFC PF NPS Equity Advantage/Surakshit Income, ICICI NPS DREAM/MFMF, UTI Dynamic Asset Allocator/Wealth Builder, Tata Smart Retirement, Axis NPS Gold, DSP NPS Long Term Equity, Kotak NPS K...)

scheme_code_format.pattern: SMxxxxxx (e.g. SM001003 = SBI Pension Fund Scheme E Tier I). First 3 digits after 'SM' = PFM number (001=SBI, 002=UTI, 003=LIC, 005=Kotak, 007=ICICI, 008=HDFC, 010=Aditya Birla, 011=Tata, 012=Max Life[discontinued], 013=Axis, 014=DSP). Confirmed directly against live NPS Trust data, not just third-party listings.

unified_pension_scheme_ups.eligibility: Central Govt employees under NPS as of 1 April 2025; new CG recruits from that date; certain retirees who superannuated/retired on or before 31 March 2025 with >=10 years qualifying service.
unified_pension_scheme_ups.contribution_structure: Employee 10% of Basic Pay+DA; Government matching 10%; additional Government contribution ~8.5% of Basic Pay+DA into a pooled 'Pool Corpus'.
unified_pension_scheme_ups.assured_payout: 50% of last-12-month average basic pay at superannuation after >=25 years qualifying service (proportionate for 10-25 years); minimum guaranteed payout Rs 10,000/month after 10 years service; family payout = 60% of subscriber's payout.
unified_pension_scheme_ups.investment_choice: Individual corpus invested in NPS-style schemes (LC25/LC50/Default originally; LC75 and Balanced-LC extended to UPS in Oct 2025); benchmark-corpus mechanism compares individual-corpus outcome against assured payout, shortfall must be replenished by subscriber to receive the assured payout.
unified_pension_scheme_ups.nav_evidence: UPS CG SCHEME (SM001017) and UPS POOL CG SCHEME (SM001018) for SBI PFM confirmed present with live NAVs (10.4998 and 10.3793 respectively) in nav-report-excel data pulled 2026-09-27.

nps_vatsalya.launched: 18 September 2024 (Guidelines 2025 formally issued/press-released 9 January 2026, superseding the original Sept-2024 circular)
nps_vatsalya.eligibility: Any Indian citizen (incl. NRI/OCI minors) under 18; account opened and operated by guardian; minor is sole beneficiary; PRAN in minor's name.

contribution.note_on_conflicting_figures: Two different minimum-contribution figures found in official sources and NOT reconciled in the time available - FLAGGED AS A GAP.

figure_B_2025_guidelines_press_release.note: Dated 9 Jan 2026 - more recent than figure_A; RECOMMEND using this figure but verify against live PFRDA site before shipping.

nps_vatsalya.on_majority_18yo: Continues under Vatsalya up to age 21 unless subscriber opts to exit or shift; fresh KYC required; if corpus <= Rs 8 lakh: full withdrawal option; if corpus > Rs 8 lakh: up to 80% lump sum, minimum 20% annuity. If no option exercised by 21, account auto-shifts to a higher-equity MSF variant and is thereafter governed by the standard Exit Regulations.
nps_vatsalya.note_on_older_exit_figure: An older FAQ page states a different exit threshold (corpus <= Rs 2.5 lakh for full withdrawal, else minimum 80% annuity) - superseded by the Dec-2025 Exit Regulations amendment and the newer scheme page; use the Rs 8 lakh / 80:20 figures above.
nps_vatsalya.partial_withdrawal: After 3 years from account opening; up to 25% of own contributions (excluding returns); for minor's education, treatment of specified illness, or disability >75%; max twice before 18 and twice more between 18-21.

tax.old_regime: Contribution deductible up to Rs 50,000 under Section 80CCD(1B) when made by parent/guardian; partial withdrawal up to 25% of own contribution exempt under Section 10(12BA); lump-sum on exit up to 60% of corpus exempt.

tier2_tax_saver_scheme_tts.min_contribution: Rs 1,000 to activate; Rs 250 minimum subsequent contribution.
tier2_tax_saver_scheme_tts.lock_in: 3 years from the date of credit of EACH contribution (rolling lock-in per contribution, not per account); cannot be assigned/pledged/hypothecated during lock-in.
tier2_tax_saver_scheme_tts.tax_treatment: Deduction under Section 80C (i.e. within the standard Rs 1.5 lakh 80C/80CCE ceiling, NOT under 80CCD) - notified as 'National Pension Scheme Tier II - Tax Saver Scheme, 2020' under Section 80C(2)(xxv) of the Income-tax Act.

tier1_all_citizen_model.min_annual_total: Rs 1,000 (else account is 'frozen' until reactivated with minimum contribution + Rs 100/year-of-default penalty)
tier1_all_citizen_model.entry_age: 18 to 70 years for individual (All Citizen Model) at account opening.

tier2_all_citizen_model.prerequisite: Active Tier I account required before opening Tier II.
tier2_all_citizen_model.tax_treatment: None - no deduction on contribution, no special tax treatment on gains; taxed at subscriber's marginal rate; withdrawal unrestricted at any time.
tier2_all_citizen_model.one_way_transfer: Tier II -> Tier I transfer allowed; Tier I -> Tier II NOT allowed.

employer_contribution_tax_treatment.for_employer: Employer's own contribution deductible as a business expense under Section 36(1)(iva) of the Income-tax Act, up to 10% of Basic+DA.
employer_contribution_tax_treatment.for_employee: Employer's contribution to the employee's NPS account is deductible by the EMPLOYEE under Section 80CCD(2), separate from and in addition to the Rs 1.5 lakh 80CCE ceiling (see tax_treatment section for current % limits).

government_sector_standard_nps.government_matching_contribution: 14% of Basic Pay + DA (raised from 10% to 14% for Central Govt employees effective 1 April 2019).
government_sector_standard_nps.note: Distinct from the Unified Pension Scheme (UPS) contribution structure - see scheme_universe.unified_pension_scheme_ups.

tax_treatment.note: Only what official/near-official sources state for FY2025-26 (AY2026-27); Income-tax Act 2025 (effective AY2026-27) renumbers Section 80CCD as Section 124 but keeps the same substance per secondary tax-guide sources - not independently verified against the Act text itself (GAP).

own_contribution_80ccd1.limit: 10% of salary (Basic+DA) for salaried employees, or 20% of gross total income for self-employed individuals; counts INSIDE the overall Rs 1.5 lakh ceiling of Section 80CCE (shared with 80C/80CCC).

additional_own_contribution_80ccd1b.limit: Additional Rs 50,000, exclusively for NPS Tier I (and APY) contributions, over and above the Rs 1.5 lakh 80CCE ceiling.

employer_contribution_80ccd2.available_in: BOTH old and new tax regime - the only NPS-related deduction that survives in the new regime.

limit_private_sector_employees.new_regime: 14% of salary (Basic+DA) - raised from 10% by Budget/Finance Act 2024, effective FY2025-26 (AY2026-27), to align with government employees.

employer_contribution_80ccd2.rupee_cap: None (pure percentage of salary), but subject to the aggregate-perquisite rule below.
employer_contribution_80ccd2.aggregate_perquisite_rule: If the EMPLOYER's combined annual contribution to EPF + NPS + superannuation fund exceeds Rs 7.5 lakh, the excess AND notional interest/growth on the excess is taxable as a perquisite under Section 17(2)(vii).

citation.cross_checked_against: https://www.pfrda.org.in/documents/33652/217954/A+Guide+to+Tax+Savings+Through+NPS.pdf (official PFRDA guide, describes the pre-Budget-2024 10%/14% baseline; does not yet reflect the FY2025-26 14%-for-private-sector-new-regime change, so the tax-guide sites were used for that specific recent change)

exit_taxation_all_citizen_tier1.lump_sum_at_exit: Up to 60% of total corpus withdrawn as lump sum at exit is exempt under Section 10(12A) of the Income-tax Act (this is the LEGACY 60% figure tied to the pre-Dec-2025 60:40 default; with the Dec-2025 amendment allowing up to 80% lump sum for non-government subscribers, verify whether Section 10(12A)'s exemption cap has been correspondingly updated to 80% - NOT independently confirmed in the time available, FLAGGED AS A GAP).
exit_taxation_all_citizen_tier1.annuity_purchase_amount: Amount used to purchase the annuity is not taxed at the time of purchase; the periodic annuity/pension income received later is taxed as income in the year of receipt.

exit_rules.effective_regulation: PFRDA (Exits and Withdrawals under the NPS) Regulations, 2015, as last amended 20 July 2026 (consolidated text); major overhaul via the PFRDA (Exits and Withdrawals under the NPS) (Amendment) Regulations, 2025, notified 12 December 2025.
exit_rules.gap_note: A further amendment dated 20 July 2026 exists (title only found: 'PFRDA (Exits and Withdrawals under the National Pension System) (Amendment) Regulations, 2026') - its specific incremental changes beyond the Dec-2025 overhaul were NOT itemised in the time available. The rule figures below are as stated in the Dec-2025 amendment press release and sector FAQ PDFs; always re-check the live consolidated PDF before relying on these figures for the simulator.

definitions.normal_exit: All Citizen Model: on completing 15 years of subscription OR reaching 60 years of age, whichever is EARLIER (changed from 'only at 60' by the Dec-2025 amendment). Government/Corporate Sector: on superannuation/retirement.
definitions.vesting_period: Subscription period required to become eligible for normal exit.
definitions.premature_exit: Exit before completing the vesting period.
definitions.lock_in_period: Subscription period required to become eligible for premature exit (typically 3 years for All Citizen Model).

government_sector.corpus_gt_8_le_12_lakh: up to Rs 6 lakh lump sum, balance via Systematic Unit Redemption (SUR, min. 6 years) or annuity, or the standard 60:40 split

all_citizen_and_corporate_sector.lump_sum: up to 80% (RAISED from 60% by Dec-2025 amendment)
all_citizen_and_corporate_sector.corpus_gt_8_le_12_lakh: up to Rs 6 lakh lump sum + balance via SUR/annuity, OR the 80:20 split

deferment.rule: Subscriber may defer lump-sum withdrawal and/or annuity purchase up to age 85 (RAISED from 75 by the Dec-2025 amendment) by submitting a request to NPS Trust/authorized intermediary; may exit any time during deferment.

citation.publisher: Indian Express, reporting the PFRDA amendment

premature_voluntary_exit_before_60_all_c.vesting_period_before_normal_exit: None specifically for 'voluntary' exit category beyond the general 3-year lock-in from account opening.
premature_voluntary_exit_before_60_all_c.corpus_gt_5_lakh: up to 20% lump sum; minimum 80% must be annuitised.
premature_voluntary_exit_before_60_all_c.note: This restrictive 20:80 split for early/voluntary exit appears UNCHANGED by the Dec-2025 amendment (which focused on normal exit and post-60 joiners) - the 80:20 liberalisation applies to NORMAL exit (60/15yr) and to individuals joining after 60, not to early voluntary exit before the vesting period.

individuals_joining_after_age_60.vesting_period: REMOVED entirely by the Dec-2025 amendment (previously 3 years).
individuals_joining_after_age_60.corpus_le_12_lakh: 100% lump-sum option available (raised from a Rs 5 lakh threshold).

before_60_or_before_superannuation.eligibility: after 3 years from date of subscription
before_60_or_before_superannuation.amount: up to 25% of OWN contributions, excluding any appreciation/returns

after_60_or_after_superannuation.eligibility: immediately, subject to 3-year subscription already completed
after_60_or_after_superannuation.amount: up to 25% (excluding returns) of the relevant contribution stream(s)

payout_mechanisms: Systematic Unit Redemption (SUR) - minimum 6 years, used for the 'balance after Rs 6 lakh lump sum' band
Annuity via PFRDA-empanelled Annuity Service Providers (ASPs)
exit_rules.annuity_mandatory: Yes, in general, except in the small-corpus 100%-lump-sum exception bands noted above. Default annuity choice is only mandatory for death/missing-presumed-dead exits; otherwise subscriber selects ASP and annuity type freely.

lifecycle_funds.framework_note: Auto Choice and Active Choice were together renamed 'Common Schemes (CS)' by circular PFRDA/2025/09/REG-PF/01 dated 16 September 2025, as part of the Multiple Scheme Framework (MSF) rollout.

glide_path_asset_allocation.note: E=Equity, C=Corporate Bonds, G=Government Securities. Percentages at key ages, per PIB press release 24 Oct 2025 Annexure (extending LC75/BLC to Central Govt employees under NPS & UPS).

up_to_35_years.LC_Aggressive_BLC: E:50%, C:30%, G:20% (tapering starts later, at 45, than LC75)

at_45_years.LC25_Low: E:15%, C:25%, G:60% (approx, tapering already underway)
at_45_years.LC_Aggressive_BLC: still near peak equity (tapering begins at 45)

citation.publisher: Press Information Bureau, Govt of India, reporting PFRDA/DoPPW decision

glide_path_asset_allocation.gap: The full year-by-year tapering matrix (age 35 through 55, one row per year) is published as an image/chart in the official PFRDA circular (npstrust.org.in/sites/default/files/circulars-documents/Circular-1.pdf, Annexure II) but was extracted as raw chart-axis numbers, not a clean age->allocation table, in the time available - a production simulator needs to re-derive/digitize the exact per-year glide path from that PDF's chart rather than rely on the 3 milestone-age snapshots captured here.

default_scheme_asset_allocation_governme.equity: up to 25% (increased from a lower cap effective 1 April 2025)

active_choice_caps.equity_E: up to 75% (Tier I) / up to 100% (Tier II)

multiple_nav_framework_2026.reason: Differentiated Investment Management Fee (IMF) for Government vs Non-Government subscribers (per circular PFRDA/2026/15/REG-PF/04 dated 6 March 2026), and Point-of-Presence (POP) distributor charges for common schemes (incl. NPS Vatsalya, NPS Lite) now adjusted directly through NAV rather than charged separately (per circulars PFRDA/2026/16/REG-POP/01 and PFRDA/2026/17/REG-POP/02 dated 10 March 2026).
multiple_nav_framework_2026.effect: A single underlying scheme can now have MULTIPLE parallel NAVs depending on subscriber channel/category (e.g. 'DIRECT'/e-NPS vs 'POP'-distributed, and Government vs Non-Government). Empirically confirmed: SBI Scheme E Tier I NAV series is continuous in value across 31-March-2026 -> 1-April-2026 but the scheme code/name changes from SM001003 'SBI PENSION FUND SCHEME E - TIER I' to SM001025 'NPS TRUST A/C SBI PENSION FUND SCHEME E - TIER I DIRECT'.
multiple_nav_framework_2026.simulator_implication: The simulator must pick ONE consistent NAV series per scheme going forward (recommend the 'DIRECT'/e-NPS series, since that is what a self-directed retail user opening an account online would be on) and document that pre-April-2026 history and post-April-2026 'DIRECT' history are being spliced together as one continuous series.

other_notable_2025_2026_changes.change: Multiple Scheme Framework (MSF) for non-government subscribers introduced.
Standardised classification/naming framework for all schemes (Categories A-E by equity-exposure band) mandated for subscriber-facing interfaces.
Six Auto-Choice investment options now available to Central Government subscribers (expanded from 4), per Gazette Notification 13 Nov 2025.
